title: I love nature, so I made a small, calm game about it. My first collection is butterflies. Every one comes from a real natural history drawing. Big shout-out to Opus.
author: mertuner
selftext:
I’ve loved nature for as long as I can remember and I wanted a quiet way to share that. The Quiet Cabinet is my small attempt. The next collection that I've already planned is going to be birds.

It’s a gentle sorting puzzle: you move butterflies into wooden specimen cases until each case holds one species. That’s all. But while you play, you get to know them. After a chapter, you can tell a Brimstone from an Orange tip, or a Peacock from a Red Admiral, without ever having sat down to study.

You sort them into cases and get to know 64 real species along the way, each from a natural history plate, each with its own Field Guide page. No timers, no ads and most importantly no rush. The first chapter is free. 

Every butterfly that lands plays a note, and every case you complete adds an instrument, so each puzzle ends as its own small piece

I'd hear your feedback. Any feedback'd be much appreciated.

PS: If you liked the game, let me know; I can give you a promo code to access the full butterfly collection. 

Thanks in advance!
